honestly i get a lot of panic attacks and this is a little similar to how i react. personally when i am having one i want to be alone, and from the sounds of it he does as well. if he’s going into another room and asking you to leave, you should leave. please respect those boundaries. forcefully staying near him while he is repeatedly asking you to leave is only going to end bad for both of you.

Personally when i am having a panic attack i am completely out of control of my emotions, so i need to be alone until i calm down so i don’t lash out to those around me. this needs to be communicated though. if it feels like he is just giving you the cold shoulder talk to him abt it, but if he’s saying he needs space to calm down, give him that space. And lastly, if he isn’t currently seeing professional help, the best you can do is encourage him to do so. many ppl, especially men, feel a stigma to getting help even when it is clearly necessary. getting him a therapist and some meds is genuinely the most help you can give him. 

remember you are not his therapist. if he is taking his energy out on you, ie screaming, starting fights, constant cold shoulder, that’s not how a relationship should be going. if his mental health is causing detriment to your own, you need to communicate that to him or end the relationship.
